newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - U.S. NAPM worth a glance Sept 30 week.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - U.S. NAPM worth a glance Sept 30 week.

text.p: Next Friday's employment report will eclipse the rest of the economic calendar next week, but a key manufacturing-sector survey and new home sales will also be observed with a keen eye, according to U.S. economists in a Reuters poll.
On average, 26 experts forecast 166,000 new jobs were created in September, down from 250,000 in August.
Taking second billing next week will be the National Association of Purchasing Management's (NAPM) index.
The economists forecast the September survey of manufacturing activity dropped to a modest 52.5, down from 52.6 in August.
Individual components of the report will have more relevance than its headline number, said Steve Ricchiuto, chief financial economist at BZW Securities Inc.

"You had an uptick in the Philadelphia (Fed survey) price components that got people thinking the (Federal Reserve) might tighten," said Ricchiuto, adding that an uptick in the price components of the NAPM survey could prompt the Fed to take action in the near future.
"Remember, those were the type of measures that got the Fed tightening in 1994," he added.
The NAPM index is set for release on Tuesday, October 1 at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT.
Marilyn Schaja, money market economist at DLJ Securities Corp, said the August new homesales number -- due out Monday -- could be a telltale sign to a slowdown in the economy.

"We've gotten some mixed indications on the housing sector and it is one of the important vectors in terms of the anticipation whether we are seeing a slowdown or not, or how significant the slowdown will be."
